rounds.text: Easun Capital Markets Ltd is undergoing a powerful fundamental inflection, demonstrated by a massive 154% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 53% surge in trailing sales growth [E17, E21]. This momentum is corroborated by accelerating earnings and a dramatic 183% year-on-year net profit jump, proving that the business's recent operational performance vastly outpaces its historical averages [E44, E46]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free, providing a pristine balance sheet that eliminates financial distress risk while it scales [E41]. Market pricing remains reasonable relative to asset backing, with a price-to-book ratio of 1.26x that trades in line with the sector benchmark of 1.29x [E7]. Management confidence is firmly intact as well, with promoter holding steady at 49.27% over the long term, showing stable alignment with the equity [E33]. Conceded: [E29], [E30], [E31] show that operating and free cash flow for March 2026 are negative at Rs -0.41 Cr with a weak cash conversion of -1.71x.

Easun Capital Markets Ltd trades at a rich P/E of 43.6x [E1], which heavily outpaces the sector benchmark of 18.76x [E6], while its EV/EBITDA of 29.49x likewise dwarfs the sector benchmark of 13.11x [E11]. This expensive valuation is completely disconnected from the firm's weak underlying profitability, evidenced by an ROE of just 1.1% [E13] and an ROCE of 1.3% [E12], both lagging far behind respective sector benchmarks of 4.91% [E9] and 5.42% [E10]. Long-term wealth creation has been negative, as demonstrated by a 10-year compounded profit growth of -12% [E18] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of -22% [E19]. Furthermore, cash generation has broken down completely, with operating and free cash flows dropping to negative Rs 0.41 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of -1.71x for Mar 2026 [E29, E30, E31]. The fundamental mismatch leaves the stock carrying an extreme DCF overvaluation of -311.4% [E36], with a reverse DCF implying an unjustified 18.8% earnings growth against a base case of zero [E37]. conceded: [E17]

The bear focuses heavily on historical profit contractions like the 10-year rate of -12% [E18] and 5-year rate of -22% [E19], but completely ignores the massive, accelerating pivot happening right now, where trailing twelve-month profit growth has exploded by 154% [E21] and net profit is up 183% YoY [E44]. While the bear cites high valuation multiples such as the 43.6x P/E [E1] and 29.49x EV/EBITDA [E11], these rearview metrics fail to capture a business whose recent quarterly profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 143%, signaling an emerging operational turnaround that makes stale historical ratios obsolete [E39, E50]. Furthermore, the bear flags an alarming ROE of 1.1% [E13] and negative cash flows [E30, E31], but overlooks that the company is almost debt free [E41], boasts a superior Return on Assets of 2.83% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.9% [E8], and has seen its 3-year compounded sales growth surge to 29% [E16] alongside a 53% spike over the trailing twelve months [E17]. conceded: [E1] conceded: [E11] conceded: [E36]

While the bull trumpets a trailing twelve-month profit growth explosion of 154% [E21] and a net profit increase of 183% YoY [E44], these short-term figures arrive against a bleak backdrop of a 10-year profit contraction of -12% [E18] and a 5-year profit contraction of -22% [E19]. The bull dismisses the 43.6x P/E [E1] and 29.49x EV/EBITDA [E11] as rearview metrics, yet the reverse DCF indicates that today's price of ₹ 55 already bakes in an aggressive 18.8% future earnings growth expectation that completely defies the 0.0% base-case reality [E2, E37]. Conceded: [E21]. Conceded: [E44]. Although the bull highlights a debt-free balance sheet [E41] and superior Return on Assets [E8], the company's operating and free cash flows have collapsed to a negative Rs -0.41 Cr alongside a cash conversion ratio of -1.71x for Mar 2026 [E29, E30, E31]. Furthermore, pointing to accelerating sales growth [E16, E17] cannot mask a chronically depressed median return on equity that has languished at a mere 1% over the last 3 years and 2% over 5 years, falling drastically short of the 4.91% sector benchmark [E9, E26, E27].
